newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian stocks expected to face selling-pressure.
newsitem.headline: Belgian stocks expected to face selling-pressure.

text.p: Belgium's blue-chip share index, which on Wednesday closed above the 2,000 level for the first time, was expected to come under pressure in coming days on profit-taking.
"I don't think we can maintain this level," said trader Tim Rovencamp at brokerage Nedee & Co.
The Bel-20 share index closed up 0.70 percent, or 13.87 points, at 2,005.37 after touching 2,006.45 in earlier trade.
The volume of Belgian shares traded was a heavy 3.08 billion francs.
"There are very big sellers when the index goes above 2,000," Rovencamp said.
Another trader said that any correction on the Dow would push the Bel-20 down and he didn't expect the bourse to remain bullish in the short term. The Dow was lower as the Belgian market closed.
But dealers said the Bel-20 could maintain its level if the dollar remained strong.
"We didn't expect such a high dollar and if it remains this high we have to revise our earnings prospects and the Bel-20 target for 1997," a dealer said.
Dealers said chemical stocks still remained the favourite shares among high quality stocks as profits in European chemical firms were expected to be higher in 1997.
"Chemical stocks are still good at this price level because of expected price earnings...and 1997 looks set to be a fine year for companies that are becoming less cyclical," a dealer said.
Cement maker CBR was seen rising further after closing up 1.25 percent to 3,240 francs.
"CBR is still worth buying as it's still cheaper than its European peers and it's a quality stock," said Carl Coppietirs at Fortis Investment Belgium.
Chemical and drugs group UCB, which closed down 0.15 percent to 90,050 francs after five winning sessions, was seen to be expensive by many dealers.

"When you compare UCB with European competitors it's way too expensive, but as long as the market is positive it will not come under pressure. When the market gets nervous UCB will be hit very hard," Coppietirs said.
Non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere was up 4.47 percent to 2,220 francs, ending a downward trend that started last September.
Dealers said the stock was up because of investors shopping around for shares which had recently lagged the market.
"Union Minere's performance will depend a lot on zinc prices and the dollar's strength and if it remains at this level the share should rise further," said one trader.
But he added that he was negative on the prospects for the U.S. dollar in 1997.
Bank Banque Lambert Bruxelles gained 3.06 percent to 7,080 francs after lagging recently.
